sentences.text:
For Non-Applicant : Ms. Meena Shastri, Additional. A.G.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput
 Order On Board
20.01.2023
 1.
This is a first bail application under Section 439 of CrPC for grant of regular bail.

Applicant is in jail since 15.11.2022 in connection with Crime No. 324/2022 registered at Police Station- Kondagaon,
District- Kondagaon (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2) (N) of the IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act.

2. The case of prosecution in brief, is that the complainant lodged a report alleging that the applicant committed sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix on the false pretext of marriage thereafter said offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has not committed any offence and has been falsely implicated in the case.

He next submits that the prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and there is no evidence to support the prosecution case and applicant is in jail since 15.11.2022 and still trial is not concluded, the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and submits that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of commission of offence and looking to the nature of allegation.

Raju vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86331024/
1
Therefore, he is not entitled for grant of bail.

5. Prosecutrix and her father appeared before this Court through video conferencing from DLSA,
Kondagaon and they have no objection for grant of bail to the applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and considered their rival submissions.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, looking to the statement of prosecutrix recorded before the Court and looking to the fact that applicant is in jail since 15.11.2022 and trial may take some time, without commenting anything on merits I am inclined to allow this bail application.

8. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- along with one surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court on the condition that - a) He shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court.
b) He is restrained from meeting any prosecution witnesses.
c) He shall not involve himself in any offence of similar nature in future.

d) He shall not temper with the evidence or influence the witnesses.
9.

It is made clear that the observations made herein above is only for the purpose of deciding the bail application and the trial Court will decide the case on its own merits without being influenced by any observation made herein above.

It is also made clear that the victim/complainant or State is at liberty to move an application regarding cancellation of bail of the applicant in the event of applicant involving himself in similar offence in future or violates any of the conditions.
10. Certified copy as per rules.
